library(tidyverse)

# Examining the Melbourne Housing data
Data is provided here: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/anthonypino/melbourne-housing-market

Uses MELBOURNE_HOUSE_PRICES_LESS

## Making sure the data is in a good format

```{r}
mhData <- read_csv("data/MELBOURNE_HOUSE_PRICES_LESS.csv")

# Date sold split into components
mhData <- mhData %>% separate_wider_delim(cols = Date,delim = "/", names = c("Day", "Month", "Year"), cols_remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Day, Month, Year), as.numeric)) %>%
  # Making some cols factors
  # possibly could bin postcodes and make it a factor, but not sure if binned codes are related to one another
  mutate(across(c(Rooms, Type, Method, Regionname, CouncilArea, Day, Month, Year), as.factor)) # probably dont care about day being a factor

# Labels
mhData$MethodLab <- factor(mhData$Method, levels = levels(mhData$Method), labels = c("Passed in", "Sold prior not disclosed", "Sold", "Sold after auction", "Sold not disclosed", "Sold prior", "Sold after auction, not disclosed", "Vendor bid" , "Withdrawn"))

mhData$Type <- factor(mhData$Type, levels = levels(mhData$Type), labels = c("house", "townhouse", "unit"))

if (!file.exists("data/mhData.rds")) {
  saveRDS(mhData, file = "data/mhData.rds")
}

```


## Examples of contingency tables

### One way

```{r}
table(mhData$Rooms)
```
```{r}
table(mhData$MethodLab)
```

### Two way

```{r}
table(mhData$Regionname, mhData$Year)
```

```{r}
table(mhData$Month, mhData$Regionname)
```

### Summaries for quantitative variables at levels of categorical variables

```{r}
summaryQ <- function(df, group, var) {
  df %>%
    group_by({{group}}) %>%
    summarize(
      n = n(),
      mean = mean({{var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd = sd({{var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      median = median({{var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      min = min({{var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      max = max({{var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

```


```{r}
summaryQ(mhData, Type, Distance)
```

```{r}
summaryQ(mhData, Rooms, Price)
```

### Some plots

```{r}
ggplot(mhData, aes(x = Distance)) + geom_histogram(bins = 25) + 
  xlab("Distance in km from Central Business District (CBD)") +
  labs(title = "Count of sold property's distance from CBD",
       subtitle = "Uses Bins = 25") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggplot(mhData, aes(x = Month, fill = Regionname)) + geom_bar() + 
  facet_wrap(~Year) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d("Region") +
  labs(title = "Number of properties sold per month by year",
       x = "Month") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggplot(mhData, aes(x = Type, y = Distance)) + geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(title = "Distance (km) distribution by property type") +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
ggplot(mhData, aes(x = Distance, y = Price, color = Method)) + geom_point(na.rm = TRUE, alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(~ Year) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6)) +
  labs(title = "Property prices tend to be higher closer to Melbourne's CBD, regardless of year", 
       x = "Distance from CBD (km)",
       y = "Price (AUD Millions)") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Method", option = "C") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggplot(mhData, aes(x = Method, fill = Type )) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Most properties are sold",
       x = "Sell method") +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
ggplot(mhData, aes(x = reorder(CouncilArea, CouncilArea, length))) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Which councils have the most properities sold",
       x = "Council Area") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal()
```


# New plot

```{r}
library(ggbeeswarm)
ggplot(mhData,aes(Year, Price, color = Type)) + geom_quasirandom(na.rm = TRUE, alpha = 0.5) + 
  labs(title = "Variation in property prices across years by type", 
       y = "Price (AUD Millions)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6)) +
  theme_minimal()
```
